message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to the most popular public APIs that let you look up an IP address and return “company”‑level data (owner, organization, contact info, etc.).  
All of them expose a simple REST endpoint that accepts an IP address (or a CIDR block) and returns JSON.  I’ve grouped them by pricing model, key features, and typical use‑case so you can pick the one that best fits your needs.

| # | Service | Free Tier | Paid Plans | Key Features | Typical Use‑Case |
|---|---------|-----------|------------|--------------|------------------|
| 1 | **ipinfo.io** | 50k requests/month (limited fields) | $5–$200/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, company name, domain, postal code, timezone, carrier, and optional “org” field. | Quick lookup for marketing, fraud detection, or analytics dashboards. |
| 2 | **ipstack.com** | 10k requests/month (basic fields) | $10–$500/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, currency, language, time zone, ASN, carrier, and optional “organization” field. | E‑commerce fraud prevention, localized content. |
| 3 | **ipapi.co** | 30k requests/month (basic fields) | $9–$300/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, organization, domain, postal code, timezone, and optional “org” field. | Real‑time visitor profiling, compliance checks. |
| 4 | **ipgeolocation.io** | 30k requests/month (basic fields) | $10–$400/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, organization, domain, postal code, timezone, and optional “org” field. | Fraud detection, IP reputation scoring. |
| 5 | **ipwhois.io** | 10k requests/month (basic fields) | $5–$200/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, organization, domain, postal code, timezone, and optional “org” field. | IP reputation, threat intelligence. |
| 6 | **ip2location.com** | 10k requests/month (basic fields) | $10–$500/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, organization, domain, postal code, timezone, and optional “org” field. | Geo‑targeting, compliance. |
| 7 | **ipqualityscore.com** | 10k requests/month (basic fields) | $10–$500/mo (unlimited, extra fields) | Geo‑location, ASN, carrier, organization, domain, postal code, timezone, and optional “org” field. | Fraud detection, bot mitigation. |

> **NOTE:** All of the above services expose an “organization” or “org” field that contains the company name (and sometimes the contact email/phone).  Some also provide a “domain” field that can be used to perform a reverse WHOIS lookup for more detailed contact info.

---

## How to Call These APIs

Below is a generic example that works for most of the services listed above.  Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with the key you receive after signing up.

```python
import requests

def lookup_ip(ip_address: str, api_key: str, provider: str = "ipinfo") -> dict:
    """
    Generic IP lookup helper.
    
    Parameters:
        ip_address (str): The IPv4 or IPv6 address to look up.
        api_key (str): Your API key for the chosen provider.
        provider (str): One of the providers in the table above.
    
    Returns:
        dict: Parsed JSON response from the provider.
    """
    base_urls = {
        "ipinfo": f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip_address}/json?token={api_key}",
        "ipstack": f"https://api.ipstack.com/{ip_address}?access_key={api_key}",
        "ipapi": f"https://ipapi.co/{ip_address}/json/?key={api_key}",
        "ipgeolocation": f"https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey={api_key}&ip={ip_address}",
        "ipwhois": f"https://ipwhois.app/json/{ip_address}?key={api_key}",
        "ip2location": f"https://api.ip2location.io?key={api_key}&ip={ip_address}",
        "ipqualityscore": f"https://www.ipqualityscore.com/api/json/ip/{api_key}/{ip_address}"
    }

    url = base_urls.get(provider)
    if not url:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported provider: {provider}")

    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

# Example usage:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    ip = "8.8.8.8"
    key = "YOUR_API_KEY"
    data = lookup_ip(ip, key, provider="ipinfo")
    print(data)
```

### Sample Response (ipinfo.io)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country": "US",
  "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840",
  "postal": "94035",
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "org": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "asn": "AS15169",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "email": "support@google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000"
  }
}
```

> **Tip:** The `company` object is optional and only appears if the provider has enriched data for that IP.  For many IPs, especially residential ones, the `org` field will contain the ISP or hosting provider rather than a “company” name.

---

## Choosing the Right Provider

| Criteria | ipinfo.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipgeolocation.io | ipwhois.io |
|----------|-----------|-------------|----------|------------------|------------|
| **Free Tier** | 50k req/month | 10k req/month | 30k req/month | 30k req/month | 10k req/month |
| **Geo‑Location Accuracy** | Very good (up-to-date database) | Good | Good | Good | Good |
| **Company Data** | Yes (via `company` field) | Yes (via `org` field) | Yes (via `org` field) | Yes (via `org` field) | Yes (via `org` field) |
| **Contact Info** | Email & phone (optional) | Not always available | Not always available | Not always available | Not always available |
| **Rate Limits** | 1,000 req/min (paid) | 1,000 req/min (paid) | 1,000 req/min (paid) | 1,000 req/min (paid) | 1,000 req/min (paid) |
| **Pricing (Unlimited)** | $5/mo | $10/mo | $9/mo | $10/mo | $5/mo |
| **Best For** | Marketing & analytics | E‑commerce fraud | Real‑time profiling | Fraud detection | Threat intelligence |

> **Bottom line:** If you need *contact* details (email/phone) for the company owning the IP, **ipinfo.io** is the most reliable source.  For a cheaper alternative that still gives you the organization name, **ipstack.com** or **ipapi.co** are solid choices.

---

## Privacy & Compliance

- **GDPR**: When collecting IP addresses, you’re dealing with personal data under GDPR.  Make sure you have a lawful basis (e.g., legitimate interest or consent) and that you store the data securely.
- **Data Retention**: Most providers allow you to set a retention period for your logs.  Keep it short (e.g., 30 days) unless you have a business reason to keep it longer.
- **User Consent**: If you’re displaying company data on a website, consider adding a notice that you’re using a third‑party service to enrich visitor data.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Sign up** for a free trial on the provider(s) that interest you.
2. **Test** the API with a handful of IPs to see what fields you get back.
3. **Integrate** the helper function into your codebase (or use the provider’s official SDK if available).
4. **Monitor** your usage against the free tier limits; upgrade to a paid plan if you hit the cap.

Happy coding! If you run into any issues or need help parsing the response, just let me know.
